help.intro: A category is a node in a tree, with one content entry per language holding its label, slug and description. Two separate trees live here — one for products, one for articles — and a category never crosses between them.
help.step_1_body: Product or article, chosen once: the field is locked after creation because the type decides which tree the category belongs to and how deep that tree may go — three levels for products, two for articles, counting a root as one.
help.step_2_title: Choose a parent, or leave it empty
help.step_2_body: An empty parent makes it a root. The picker only offers categories of the same type that still have room under the depth ceiling, so a choice it presents is one the save will accept.
help.step_3_title: Write the content, one language at a time
help.step_3_body: Label, slug and description are required per language. Leaving the slug empty derives it from the label, and it is lower-cased and must be unique for its type and language across every category — a non-latin label derives nothing, so type the slug yourself there.
help.step_4_body: A new category starts pending and is not public until enabled. Disabling one that still has active descendants is refused — deactivate the branch from the leaves up, because the dashboard does not force the cascade.
help.step_5_body: Order opens one sibling group at a time — the active categories under one parent, or the roots of one type — and expects the whole group in the order wanted. Moving a category or changing its status resets its position to the end of wherever it lands.
help.step_6_body: Tree is the read-only view of the hierarchy, which the flat list cannot show. Use it before a move: what has to fit under a new parent is the whole subtree, not just the category you are dragging.
help.note: Deleting is a soft delete and is refused while a descendant is still alive, so a branch comes down from the leaves up. Restoring goes the other way — a category cannot come back while its parent is deleted or inactive.
